gamla: Stockholm's medieval heart, on an island surrounded by water: narrow cobbled lanes, ochre and red houses, Stortorget square with its stepped gables and Mårten Trotzigs gränd, the city's narrowest alley (about 90 centimetres). See it on foot, taking your time.
slottet: One of Europe's largest royal residences still in use, with over six hundred rooms: the Royal Apartments, the Hall of State, the Treasury with the crowns and the Tre Kronor Museum, which shows the remains of the medieval castle that burned down in 1697. In front is the changing of the guard.
nobel: The museum of the Nobel Prizes, in the old Stock Exchange on Stortorget: the stories of the laureates, objects they donated and a small exhibition on Alfred Nobel's invention. You can see it in an hour, and the café inside is nice.
stadshuset: The great red-brick building on Lake Mälaren where the Nobel banquet is held every 10 December. It can only be visited on a guided tour of about 45 minutes, in English, which takes you into the Blue Hall and the Golden Hall, with mosaics of 18 million gold and glass tiles. The lakeside garden is free and has great views.
vasa: The Swedish warship from 1628 that sank in the harbour a few minutes into her maiden voyage and was raised 333 years later: today she's the world's only almost intact 17th-century ship, as tall as a six-storey building and covered in carvings. The museum also tells the story of life on board.
skansen: The world's oldest open-air museum, opened in 1891 on a hill on Djurgården: farms, churches and workshops from all over Sweden, with craftspeople in costume, an 18th-century town quarter and a small park with Nordic animals (elk, bears, lynx and wolves). The view of Stockholm from the hill is beautiful.
abba: An interactive museum dedicated to Sweden's most famous band: stage costumes, instruments, gold records and a booth where you can sing with hologram ABBA. It ends in the "Polar Studio" with the original mixing desk. The most fun stop if you like their songs.
fotog: A museum of contemporary photography in an early-20th-century brick building on the Södermalm waterfront: temporary exhibitions by major photographers and a top-floor restaurant with views over the water and Gamla Stan. It's open late, a nice way to end the evening.
monte: Monteliusvägen and the view from Södermalm

A panoramic path about 400 metres long on the Mariaberget hill in Södermalm, above Lake Mälaren: from there you see the City Hall, Riddarholmen, Gamla Stan and the city's rooftops. The best spot for sunset photos.
historiska: The museum of Swedish history from the Stone Age to the Vikings: the Viking exhibition with jewellery, swords and ships, and the Gold Room with over two thousand precious objects. Well done and suitable even if you know nothing about the subject.
saluhall: The city's most elegant covered market, in an 1888 brick building: stalls of fish, cheese, meat and sweets, with small restaurants where you eat standing or at the counter. From here you walk on to Strandvägen, the harbourside boulevard with grand old buildings and vintage boats moored along it.
